thread: Follow the swarm into human-made flight: first ride the air in a motorless glider, then add an engine and wings, and finally lift off on spinning rotors. Along the way, sailplanes, propellers, cockpits, and curious flying machines become creatures of their own.

candidates.name: National Soaring Museum
candidates.why: A collection of sailplanes from the 1890s onward offers long wings, flying planks, and ingenious motorless shapes, alongside soaring landmarks and the history of gliding.

candidates.name: Polish Aviation Museum in Kraków
candidates.why: Aircraft, gliders, and a whole engine hall offer radial cylinders, propellers, experimental airframes, and agricultural aircraft with distinctive working parts.

candidates.name: The Helicopter Museum
candidates.why: Helicopters and autogyros from around the world provide whirling rotors, improbable tails, open cockpits, and many different ways to rise vertically.

candidates.name: Finnish Aviation Museum
candidates.why: Finnish sailplanes and seaplanes sit alongside airliners, aviation objects, photographs, and recordings: a collection of wings, floats, instruments, and cabins.

candidates.name: South Australian Aviation Museum
candidates.why: Historic aircraft, wooden propellers, and unusual early engines offer a menagerie of spinning blades, piston arrangements, and airframes.

candidates.name: The Museum of Flight
candidates.why: Its aircraft collection, restoration work, and technical archives offer flying machines and the parts, tools, and drawings that keep them aloft.

candidates.name: Aeroflight
candidates.why: Aircraft types, manufacturers, civil aviation, and public-service operators give the swarm many wing shapes and specialized flying jobs to explore.

candidates.name: Gliding Heritage Centre
candidates.why: A volunteer-run collection of historic British gliders reveals the slim wings, light structures, and restoration craft behind silent flight.

candidates.name: Queensland Air Museum
candidates.why: Civilian and utility aircraft, aero-engines, and restoration projects offer another collection of cockpits, moving parts, and working flying machines.
